title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
why_read: A concrete empirical test of whether AI agents can genuinely reproduce and stress-test published scientific analyses, with a public benchmark.
analysis: The authors built a benchmark of 20 published cancer-registry studies and had an AI agent try to reproduce 2,190 specific factual claims from them, succeeding on about 77%. They also built a pipeline that proposes alternative reasonable analysis choices and reruns studies to see if conclusions still hold, flagging about 9.5% of findings as sensitive to those choices. This is a meaningful, measurable contribution to using LLMs for scientific quality control rather than just generation. It matters because reproducibility failures are a known crisis in science and this offers a scalable way to catch them.
